overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the committee discussed two unnoticed topics, but the chair could not have anticipated them 48 hours ahead, and the resignation was only announced, not deliberated; payroll and HIPAA issues were declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee discussed her resignation, a topic not on the April 13 notice, which was not reasonably anticipated 48 hours before the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: further find that the Committee did not actually discuss the complainant's resignation; Dr. Lally simply notified the Committee of the resignation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee discussed a Do Not Resuscitate policy at the April 13 meeting, a topic not listed on either the original or revised notice.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee was not aware of the complainant's resignation or the DNR policy until the day of the meeting, the chair could not have reasonably anticipated its discussion 48 hours prior to the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaints raised potential payroll and HIPAA issues, which are outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: thus we decline to review, and offer no opinion on, any potential payroll issues or HIPAA violations raised in the complaints.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
